tasks.title: Initialize Supabase project and configure Postgres schema
tasks.description: Create Supabase project, set up Postgres database with tables for notes, relations, and sessions. Enable Row Level Security (RLS) policies.
tasks.details:
1. Create new Supabase project via dashboard (choose US East/Southeast region)
2. Execute schema migration SQL:
   - CREATE TABLE notes with columns: id (UUID), path (TEXT UNIQUE), title, content, frontmatter (JSONB), created_at, updated_at, user_id
   - CREATE TABLE relations with columns: id, source_id (FK to notes), target_path, relation_type, context
   - CREATE TABLE sessions with columns: id, project, started_at, ended_at, summary, events (JSONB)
3. Create indexes: notes_fts (GIN for full-text search), notes_user_id, notes_path, notes_updated_at, relations_source_id, relations_target_path
4. Enable RLS on all tables: ALTER TABLE notes ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY
5. Create RLS policies for SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE filtering by auth.uid() = user_id
6. Verify schema in Supabase dashboard table editor
7. Document connection string and anon/service keys in .env.local

Pseudo-code:
```sql
CREATE TABLE notes (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  path TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  title TEXT NOT NULL,
  content TEXT NOT NULL,
  frontmatter JSONB DEFAULT '{}',
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now(),
  user_id UUID REFERENCES auth.users(id)
);

CREATE INDEX notes_fts ON notes USING gin(to_tsvector('english', title || ' ' || content));
ALTER TABLE notes ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
CREATE POLICY "Users can view own notes" ON notes FOR SELECT USING (auth.uid() = user_id);
```

tasks.title: Create data migration script from SQLite/files to Postgres
tasks.description: Build Python script to read existing .md files and SQLite data, transform to match new schema, and bulk insert into Supabase Postgres.
tasks.details:
1. Create scripts/migrate_to_supabase.py
2. Install dependencies: supabase-py, python-dotenv
3. Read all .md files from VAULT_PATH directory recursively
4. For each file:
   - Parse frontmatter (YAML) into JSONB
   - Extract wikilinks [[...]] and #tags into relations table entries
   - Generate UUID for note ID
   - Create notes table record
5. Read any existing SQLite database (if exists) for sessions data
6. Batch insert using Supabase client: supabase.table('notes').insert([...]).execute()
7. Handle conflicts (ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE) for idempotency
8. Log progress: X/Y notes migrated
9. Generate migration report: success count, errors, skipped files

Pseudo-code:
```python
import supabase
import frontmatter
import re
from pathlib import Path

client = supabase.create_client(SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_KEY)
vault = Path(VAULT_PATH)

for md_file in vault.rglob('*.md'):
    post = frontmatter.load(md_file)
    note = {
        'path': str(md_file.relative_to(vault)),
        'title': post.metadata.get('title', md_file.stem),
        'content': post.content,
        'frontmatter': post.metadata,
        'user_id': USER_ID
    }
    result = client.table('notes').insert(note).execute()
    
    # Extract wikilinks
    links = re.findall(r'\[\[(.+?)\]\]', post.content)
    for link in links:
        client.table('relations').insert({
            'source_id': result.data[0]['id'],
            'target_path': link,
            'relation_type': 'wikilink'
        }).execute()
```

4. Check random sample of notes for correct content/frontmatter
5. Verify relations extracted: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM relations WHERE relation_type='wikilink'
6. Test idempotency: Run script twice, should not duplicate data

Pseudo-code:
```python
# app/config.py
from enum import Enum
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings

class DatabaseMode(str, Enum):
    SQLITE = "sqlite"
    POSTGRES = "postgres"

class Settings(BaseSettings):
    db_mode: DatabaseMode = DatabaseMode.SQLITE
    database_url: str
    supabase_url: str = ""
    supabase_key: str = ""

# app/db.py
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import create_async_engine, async_sessionmaker

engine = create_async_engine(settings.database_url)
AsyncSessionLocal = async_sessionmaker(engine, expire_on_commit=False)

async def get_db():
    async with AsyncSessionLocal() as session:
        yield session

# app/main.py
from fastapi import FastAPI
app = FastAPI(title="Obsidian Memory API")
```

tasks.title: Implement Postgres-backed vault_manager service
tasks.description: Rewrite vault_manager.py to read/write notes from Postgres instead of file system. Support both SQLite (legacy) and Postgres modes.
tasks.details:
1. Create app/services/vault_manager.py with VaultManager class
2. Implement async methods:
   - async def get_note(path: str) -> Note
   - async def create_note(note: NoteCreate) -> Note
   - async def update_note(id: UUID, note: NoteUpdate) -> Note
   - async def delete_note(id: UUID) -> None
   - async def list_notes(user_id: UUID, limit: int = 100) -> List[Note]
3. Use SQLAlchemy async queries:
   - await session.execute(select(Note).where(Note.path == path))
   - await session.commit()
4. Handle frontmatter: Store as JSONB, parse on read if needed
5. For SQLite mode, keep legacy file-based implementation
6. Factory pattern: get_vault_manager(db_mode) returns appropriate implementation
7. Add proper error handling: NoteNotFoundError, DuplicatePathError

Pseudo-code:
```python
class PostgresVaultManager:
    def __init__(self, session: AsyncSession):
        self.session = session
    
    async def get_note(self, path: str, user_id: UUID) -> Note:
        result = await self.session.execute(
            select(NoteModel).where(
                NoteModel.path == path,
                NoteModel.user_id == user_id
            )
        )
        note = result.scalar_one_or_none()
        if not note:
            raise NoteNotFoundError(f"Note not found: {path}")
        return Note.from_orm(note)
    
    async def create_note(self, note: NoteCreate, user_id: UUID) -> Note:
        db_note = NoteModel(
            title=note.title,
            content=note.content,
            path=note.path,
            frontmatter=note.frontmatter or {},
            user_id=user_id
        )
        self.session.add(db_note)
        await self.session.commit()
        await self.session.refresh(db_note)
        return Note.from_orm(db_note)
```

tasks.title: Implement Postgres full-text search with to_tsvector
tasks.description: Rewrite search_index.py to use Postgres to_tsvector for full-text search instead of SQLite FTS5.
tasks.details:
1. Create app/services/search_index.py with SearchIndex class
2. Implement async def search(query: str, user_id: UUID, limit: int = 10) -> List[SearchResult]
3. Use Postgres full-text search:
   - Convert query to tsquery: to_tsquery('english', query)
   - Match against tsvector: WHERE to_tsvector('english', title || ' ' || content) @@ to_tsquery(...)
   - Rank results: ts_rank(to_tsvector(...), to_tsquery(...)) AS rank ORDER BY rank DESC
4. Support quoted phrases: "exact match" -> to_tsquery('exact <-> match')
5. Highlight matching snippets: ts_headline('english', content, query) for context
6. Filter by user_id for security
7. Return SearchResult with: note_id, path, title, snippet, rank
8. For SQLite mode, keep legacy FTS5 implementation

Pseudo-code:
```python
class PostgresSearchIndex:
    def __init__(self, session: AsyncSession):
        self.session = session
    
    async def search(self, query: str, user_id: UUID, limit: int = 10):
        tsquery = func.to_tsquery('english', query)
        tsvector = func.to_tsvector('english', NoteModel.title + ' ' + NoteModel.content)
        
        result = await self.session.execute(
            select(
                NoteModel.id,
                NoteModel.path,
                NoteModel.title,
                func.ts_headline('english', NoteModel.content, tsquery).label('snippet'),
                func.ts_rank(tsvector, tsquery).label('rank')
            )
            .where(
                tsvector.bool_op('@@')(tsquery),
                NoteModel.user_id == user_id
            )
            .order_by(desc('rank'))
            .limit(limit)
        )
        return [SearchResult(**row._asdict()) for row in result]
```

tasks.title: Implement graph_engine service reading from relations table
tasks.description: Rewrite graph_engine.py to query relations table for wikilinks/tags instead of parsing files.
tasks.details:
1. Create app/services/graph_engine.py with GraphEngine class
2. Implement async methods:
   - async def get_backlinks(note_id: UUID) -> List[Relation]
   - async def get_outgoing_links(note_id: UUID) -> List[Relation]
   - async def get_related_notes(note_id: UUID, max_depth: int = 2) -> Graph
   - async def get_tags(note_id: UUID) -> List[str]
3. Query relations table with JOINs:
   - Backlinks: SELECT * FROM relations r JOIN notes n ON r.source_id = n.id WHERE r.target_path = (SELECT path FROM notes WHERE id = note_id)
   - Outgoing: SELECT * FROM relations WHERE source_id = note_id
4. Build graph structure: nodes (notes) and edges (relations)
5. Support relation types: wikilink, tag, observation
6. Return RelationGraph with: nodes List[NoteNode], edges List[Edge]
7. Filter by user_id via notes.user_id

Pseudo-code:
```python
class GraphEngine:
    def __init__(self, session: AsyncSession):
        self.session = session
    
    async def get_backlinks(self, note_id: UUID, user_id: UUID):
        # Find notes that link TO this note
        target_path_subquery = select(NoteModel.path).where(NoteModel.id == note_id).scalar_subquery()
        
        result = await self.session.execute(
            select(RelationModel, NoteModel)
            .join(NoteModel, RelationModel.source_id == NoteModel.id)
            .where(
                RelationModel.target_path == target_path_subquery,
                NoteModel.user_id == user_id
            )
        )
        return [Relation.from_orm(rel) for rel, note in result]
    
    async def get_related_notes(self, note_id: UUID, user_id: UUID, max_depth: int = 2):
        # BFS traversal to build graph
        visited = set()
        queue = [(note_id, 0)]
        graph = Graph(nodes=[], edges=[])
        
        while queue:
            current_id, depth = queue.pop(0)
            if current_id in visited or depth > max_depth:
                continue
            visited.add(current_id)
            
            # Get outgoing links
            outgoing = await self.get_outgoing_links(current_id, user_id)
            for rel in outgoing:
                graph.edges.append(Edge(source=current_id, target=rel.target_id))
                if rel.target_id not in visited:
                    queue.append((rel.target_id, depth + 1))
        
        return graph
```

tasks.title: Create Obsidian export service (DB to .md files)
tasks.description: Build new service to export notes from Postgres back to .md files on disk for Obsidian compatibility.
tasks.details:
1. Create app/services/obsidian_exporter.py with ObsidianExporter class
2. Implement async def export_vault(user_id: UUID, output_path: Path) -> ExportResult
3. For each note in database:
   - Reconstruct frontmatter YAML from JSONB column
   - Write file: output_path / note.path with frontmatter + content
   - Preserve directory structure: mkdir -p for nested paths
4. Generate .obsidian/ config folder with basic settings
5. Create export metadata file: .export_metadata.json with timestamp, note count
6. Support incremental export: Only export notes modified since last export
7. Handle conflicts: Skip/overwrite/rename based on strategy parameter
8. Return ExportResult: success count, errors, skipped files, total size

Pseudo-code:
```python
import frontmatter
from pathlib import Path

class ObsidianExporter:
    def __init__(self, session: AsyncSession):
        self.session = session
    
    async def export_vault(self, user_id: UUID, output_path: Path):
        result = await self.session.execute(
            select(NoteModel).where(NoteModel.user_id == user_id)
        )
        notes = result.scalars().all()
        
        exported = 0
        for note in notes:
            file_path = output_path / note.path
            file_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            
            # Create frontmatter post
            post = frontmatter.Post(note.content)
            post.metadata = note.frontmatter or {}
            
            # Write markdown file
            with open(file_path, 'w') as f:
                f.write(frontmatter.dumps(post))
            
            exported += 1
        
        return ExportResult(success_count=exported, total_notes=len(notes))
```

tasks.title: Create FastAPI endpoints for notes CRUD operations
tasks.description: Implement RESTful API endpoints for notes: GET /notes, POST /notes, GET /notes/{id}, PATCH /notes/{id}, DELETE /notes/{id}.
tasks.details:
1. Create app/api/v1/notes.py router
2. Implement endpoints:
   - GET /api/v1/notes?limit=100&offset=0 -> List[NoteListItem]
   - POST /api/v1/notes -> Note (create new note)
   - GET /api/v1/notes/{id} -> Note (full note with content)
   - PATCH /api/v1/notes/{id} -> Note (update title/content/frontmatter)
   - DELETE /api/v1/notes/{id} -> 204 No Content
   - GET /api/v1/notes/search?q=query -> List[SearchResult]
3. Use Depends(get_db) for database session injection
4. Add authentication: Depends(get_current_user) to extract user_id from JWT
5. Validate with Pydantic schemas: NoteCreate, NoteUpdate, Note response models
6. Return 404 for not found, 403 for unauthorized access
7. Add OpenAPI documentation with examples
8. Implement pagination with Link headers

Pseudo-code:
```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException
from uuid import UUID

router = APIRouter(prefix="/api/v1/notes", tags=["notes"])

@router.get("/", response_model=List[NoteListItem])
async def list_notes(
    limit: int = 100,
    offset: int = 0,
    db: AsyncSession = Depends(get_db),
    user_id: UUID = Depends(get_current_user_id)
):
    vault = PostgresVaultManager(db)
    notes = await vault.list_notes(user_id, limit, offset)
    return notes

@router.post("/", response_model=Note, status_code=201)
async def create_note(
    note: NoteCreate,
    db: AsyncSession = Depends(get_db),
    user_id: UUID = Depends(get_current_user_id)
):
    vault = PostgresVaultManager(db)
    return await vault.create_note(note, user_id)

@router.get("/{note_id}", response_model=Note)
async def get_note(
    note_id: UUID,
    db: AsyncSession = Depends(get_db),
    user_id: UUID = Depends(get_current_user_id)
):
    vault = PostgresVaultManager(db)
    note = await vault.get_note_by_id(note_id, user_id)
    if not note:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Note not found")
    return note
```

tasks.title: Deploy and configure ElectricSQL sync service
tasks.description: Deploy Electric sync service to Fly.io, configure connection to Supabase Postgres with logical replication.
tasks.details:
1. Create Fly.io account and install flyctl CLI
2. Create fly.toml configuration for Electric service:
   - Image: electricsql/electric:latest
   - Region: Same as Supabase (e.g., iad for US East)
   - Environment variables: DATABASE_URL (Postgres connection string with IPv6 support)
3. Enable logical replication in Supabase:
   - Go to Database Settings > Replication
   - Add publication: CREATE PUBLICATION electric_publication FOR ALL TABLES
   - Verify wal_level = logical
4. Configure Electric environment variables:
   - DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres:[PASSWORD]@[SUPABASE_IPV6]:5432/postgres
   - ELECTRIC_WRITE_TO_PG_MODE=direct
   - PG_PROXY_PORT=65432
5. Deploy: fly deploy
6. Verify Electric health: curl https://[APP_NAME].fly.dev/v1/health
7. Document Electric URL in .env: ELECTRIC_URL=https://[APP_NAME].fly.dev

Pseudo-code:

# fly.toml
app = "obsidian-memory-electric"
primary_region = "iad"

[env]
  ELECTRIC_WRITE_TO_PG_MODE = "direct"
  PG_PROXY_PORT = "65432"

[[services]]
